content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

title: In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words
summary: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star, the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of […]  The post  In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. content: By Charles Gardner — We used to be regular viewers of the The Great British Bake-Off TV series, now being screened on Channel 4, celebrating the efforts of amateur contestants in the kitchen. My wife is qualified in home economics and once, in her far-off student days, helped Mary Berry out over the weekend. I too like to lend a hand with my cooking skills. So when, the other day, we were intrigued to see how new presenter Nigella Lawson was doing on the show, we switched it on – and were truly appalled at the foul language spewing out of the mouths of at least two contestants. Taking the name of the Lord Jesus Christ in vain, they loudly expressed their frustration (rather than praise) at things going wrong with their concoctions in front of more than seven million viewers. We switched it off, vowing to complain in the strongest possible terms, which I have since done. And though it’s hard to be surprised at the language regularly heard on television programmes these days, I was shocked to the core by Channel 4’s response, basically saying that this particularly offensive blasphemy doesn’t come under the category of “strong language”. Really? It’s surely the worst of them all. “We are sorry to hear you were offended by some of the language used within the programme,” they wrote. “Whilst we do appreciate that you find the use of such phrases or words unacceptable, we are not obliged under the Ofcom code to obscure them, nor do they fall under the category for strong language. We therefore have no obligation to bleep them either pre- or post-watershed.” I had suggested that they could at least have edited them out, adding that they were being very hypocritical as they wouldn’t have allowed swearing in the name of Mohammed, a point which they ignored. Have we sunk so low in our nation that there is nothing left that is sacred, except woke left-wing ideology and appeasement of those who hate the God of Israel and his Son Jesus, our Lord? But we have forsaken the God who brought peace and prosperity to Britain, and who saved us from Nazi invasion, for the idols of food and celebrity. Shame on us! Is it not time the Christian world woke up and stood against this flood of filth in our midst, which will sweep us away into the oblivion of a third-rate country if we do not act soon. Where has the ‘land of hope and glory’ gone? The ‘mother of the free’ we sing about at the Proms, calling on the God ‘who made thee mighty’ to ‘make thee mightier yet’? The Apostle Paul was surely prophesying the decline and fall of the Roman Empire in his letter to the early Christians in Rome (a mixture of Jews and Gentiles), when he wrote: “The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities – his eternal power and divine nature – have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that men are without excuse.” (Romans 1:18-20) The post Offended by foul language on food show first appeared on God Reports .

title: Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God

content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. title: Spiritual fighter pilots needed for new Battle for Britain!
summary: By Charles Gardner — The Battle of Britain, which saw Spitfires and Hurricanes save us from Nazi invasion and ensure our freedom, apparently ended after three months on October 31, 1940. content: By Charles Gardner — Barrie Clark painting of a Spitfire The Battle of Britain, which saw Spitfires and Hurricanes save us from Nazi invasion and ensure our freedom, apparently ended after three months on October 31, 1940. As we move past that date this year, many of us will no doubt be distracted by superficial celebrations like Halloween, more animated by the spectre of ghosts and witches than the real threats to our society from those who would rob us of our hard-fought freedom. Our present government would have us paralyzed with fear and trepidation as they urge us to stock up our cupboards in case of emergency, but Jesus reminds us how he takes care of the sparrows and urges us to trust him for all our needs. That wartime battle in the skies would not have been won without a nationwide turning to God in prayer, and the current challenges can only be overcome in the spiritual realm. For there is a ferocious war taking place in the heavenly places (see Ephesians 6:12) urgently requiring our participation. My Uncle Murray flew both planes mentioned above as an RAF Wing Commander during the war, and I have a painting of a Spitfire above my desk as a constant reminder of the spiritual battle we face. Tragically, an increasing section of our society are taken in by the lying propaganda of Hamas and their fellow travelers, with a jihadist agenda to rid the world of the Jewish people who brought Western civilization to the fore. The Nazi invasion we managed to prevent has come in another guise. All of which means there’s a furious battle for the soul of Britain for which we need spiritual ‘fighter pilots’ to prayerfully shoot down the archenemies of our once Christian nation by standing up for the truth Jesus came to bring us. Meanwhile left-wing activists supposedly supporting the Palestinian cause have engaged in cowardly vandalism of properties reputedly belonging to employees of companies selling military equipment to Israel. And during an anti-Israel protest in London on October 17 the Battle of Britain monument was attacked by pro-Palestinian protesters who smashed poppy wreaths dedicated to those brave men who gave their all defending our freedom. One woman was arrested after she was seen giving a Nazi salute! All these sentiments are being fuelled by our own government’s attitudes to Israel and by their cowardice in pandering to the prejudice of those whose votes they covet. But praise God for those ten thousand who have taken the trouble to sign a Christians United For Israel petition opposing sanctions on Israel. Western civilization is under serious threat. In a recent interview with the Gatestone Institute, a highly rated think tank, French documentary filmmaker Pierre Rehov was asked what Israel is really fighting for. He responded: “Israel is fighting, obviously, for its survival, but not only that. Israel is fighting to preserve Western civilization, and at a frontier the West prefers not to name: Islamic extremism and its call for global political control.” If the West rewards the October 7th, 2023, massacre with political gains, like the ‘state’ of Palestine in the midst of Israel, “it teaches a lesson to every violent movement on earth: that massacre pays”. But Israel is defending the principle that “civilization cannot survive if it negotiates with barbarity as if it were a partner who is misunderstood”. There is a tendency to pretend that “totalitarian jihadism” can be managed indefinitely, Rehov further suggested. But you either have to dismantle the infrastructure of terror “or it regrows”. If the West is defeated, he says, it will be “by the refusal to oppose danger when they see it”.(1) There is a disturbing sense of déjà vu in what we are witnessing on our streets. Even in France, where the issues of the rioters are supposedly unrelated, Jews have inevitably become the target of some of the violence. Meanwhile here in Britain, vicious antisemitic venom stalks our capital city while the police are apparent
author: Charles Gardner

title: Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith
summary: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno, in […]  The post  Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. Christopher Smart The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno , in my book Beauty (And the Banana) . I described Smart as a theopoet , someone whose deep religious convictions found expression through a distinctive and imaginative poetic vision. Smart was no ordinary poet. His writings moved freely between the sacred and the seemingly mundane, finding divine significance in everything from biblical figures to animals and the natural world. His poetry was exuberant, unconventional, and, at times, wonderfully strange. For Smart, creation itself was a chorus of praise, and every living thing had a part to play. Recently, I had another opportunity to hear Redford explore Smart’s remarkable literary legacy, this time through the music of British composer Benjamin Britten (1913–1976). As part of an All Saints’ Day concert at the Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque, New Mexico, celebrating Britten’s music, Redford delivered a pre-concert lecture focusing on the composer’s Rejoice in the Lamb , a choral masterpiece that brings Smart’s unusual poetry to life. The evening offered a fascinating intersection of literature, music, theology, and history, demonstrating how two artists separated by nearly two centuries could share a common vision of wonder. The Musical Imagination of Benjamin Britten Benjamin Britten. Photo: Public Domain. Redford, a former professor at Boston University who was living in England when Britten died in 1976, identified three defining characteristics of the composer’s work. First, Britten’s music is distinguished by “passion and variety.” His compositions resist easy categorization, moving between emotional intensity, dramatic storytelling, and moments of remarkable spiritual intimacy. Redford described Britten’s approach as creating a kind of musical parable, pointing to Curlew River , one of Britten’s church parables, as a particularly compelling example. Second, Britten demonstrated an extraordinary ability to balance “economy and scope.” Redford compared this quality to the novels of Jane Austen, whose carefully constructed narratives reveal entire worlds through seemingly modest details. Similarly, Britten could communicate profound emotional and spiritual truths through restrained musical means. Nothing was wasted; every note served a purpose. Third, and perhaps most important for the evening’s performance, Britten possessed an exceptional “sensitivity to words.” Redford described him as an “inspired” interpreter of literary texts, a composer who understood that music should not merely accompany poetry but illuminate its deeper meaning. It was this third characteristic that led Redford to Christopher Smart. When an Eccentric Poet Meets a Brilliant Composer In 1943, Britten composed Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30), a festival cantata scored for four soloists, SATB choir, and organ. The composition draws its text from Smart’s Jubilate Agno , a work of religious poetry that remained largely unknown for nearly two centuries. Christopher Smart Smart wrote much of the poem during his confinement in a private madhouse in eighteenth-century London. Its unconventional structure, biblical references, exuberant language, and seemingly spontaneous declarations of praise made it unlike almost anything else in English religious literature. The manuscript remained unpublished until W. F. Stead brought it to public attention in 1939. Soon afterward, the poet W. H. Auden introduced Britten to Smart’s newly published work while the composer was living in the United States. The connection proved fruitful. Britten recognized something remarkable in Smart’s poetry: an unrestrained celebration of creation that could be translated into music.
author: Brian Nixon
tags: Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque

title: Kehilangan yang Membawa Berkah
title_zh: 带来祝福的失去
content: Oleh: Gevonny Dinda Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Gevonny Dinda, biasa dipanggil Dinda. Sebagai orang Kristen, saya merasa bersyukur dilahirkan di dunia ini dan berkesempatan untuk mengenal Tuhan Yesus. Saya sungguh bahagia dapat merasakan berkat-Nya setiap hari dan sangat bersyukur akan apa yang Tuhan Yesus berikan kepada saya selama ini. Kabar baik, kabar buruk, cobaan, dan berkat, saya terima dengan penuh rasa ucapan syukur. Di sini, saya akan menceritakan salah satu berkat Tuhan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada 19 Februari 2015, saya menerima kabar buruk bahwa kakek saya telah berpulang ke rumah Tuhan. Kepergian kakek saya sangat membekas di hati banyak orang, terutama nenek saya. Nenek saya sangat merasa kehilangan karena memang nenek belum siap menghadapi hal ini sehingga membuat kondisi badannya melemah. Sejak ditinggal kakek, kondisi mental dan fisik nenek saya semakin memburuk. Awalnya, ia merasa sangat kesepian dan merasa takut jika ditinggal sendirian di rumah. Bahkan, nenek saya sering menangis jika merasa kesepian. Ibu saya dan ketujuh saudara kandungnya akhirnya sepakat untuk bergantian menjaga nenek saya di rumahnya supaya tidak merasa kesepian lagi. Setelah itu, hari-hari nenek saya berjalan normal seperti biasa. Namun, karena umurnya yang bertambah tua, kondisi fisiknya semakin melemah. Sejak 2017, nenek saya sudah tidak kuat lagi berjalan dan harus memakai kursi roda. Di situlah, ketabahan dan kesabaran anak-anaknya, termasuk ibu saya, diuji dalam mengurus nenek saya. Pakde, budhe, tante, dan om saya yang hidup di luar kota, seperti: Jakarta, Yogyakarta, dan Kudus, semakin sering menyempatkan diri pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bergiliran mengurus nenek saya. Sampai pada April 2018 lalu, kondisi nenek saya berada di titik terburuknya. Karena anak-anaknya sudah memiliki firasat yang tidak baik, mereka memutuskan untuk berkunjung bersama-sama ke rumah nenek saya. Mereka hanya bisa berdoa bersama untuk kondisi ibu mereka. Sampai pada akhirnya, Tuhan Yesus memanggil nenek saya untuk ikut bersama-Nya. Karena sudah siap dengan kepergian nenek saya, kami semua menerima kepergian nenek dengan sukacita dan penuh ucapan syukur karena nenek saya sudah sembuh dan pergi ke tempat yang lebih indah, menyusul kakek saya. Tidak disangka, kepergian kakek dan nenek saya membawa berkah bagi keluarga besar kami. Tuhan Yesus memiliki kuasa untuk membuat keluarga kami menjadi lebih dekat satu sama lain. Hubungan anak-anak beserta cucu-cucu mereka menjadi lebih dekat. Kakak-kakak Ibu saya yang dahulu sering pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bertemu dan menjenguk orang tua mereka, sekarang lebih menghargai waktu kebersamaan dengan keluarga yang diberikan oleh Tuhan. Sejak saat itu, kami semua memiliki satu grup chat dan sering menanyakan kabar satu sama lain. Bahkan, kami semua memiliki keinginan untuk lebih sering bertemu pada masa depan, dan melakukan kegiatan bersama-sama seperti berlibur dan arisan keluarga. Semua itu tidak pernah terjadi sebelum kepergian kakek dan nenek saya, dan saya sungguh percaya Tuhan Yesus turut campur tangan dalam semua kejadian yang menimpa keluarga saya. Ia tidak pernah berhenti untuk menunjukkan betapa sayangnya Ia terhadap anak-anak-Nya, bahkan ketika anak-anak-Nya sedang berada dalam keterpurukan. Tuhan Yesus selalu memiliki rencana yang indah untuk setiap anak-anak-Nya, dan saya sangat percaya Ia telah memberikan sesuatu yang besar untuk membalas rasa kehilangan keluarga saya selama ini. Tuhan Yesus memang sungguh baik! Semoga Tuhan selalu memberkati keluarga Anda!

title: Berbagi dengan Mengajar dan Melayani
title_zh: 通过教学和侍奉来分享
content: Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Zefanya. Saya bersyukur karena pada kesempatan ini, saya dapat menyaksikan cinta kasih Tuhan yang Ia nyatakan melalui kegiatan mengajar bahasa Inggris yang saya lakukan secara volunter untuk anak-anak di beberapa desa di sekitar kota Salatiga. Kegiatan yang diselenggarakan oleh salah satu yayasan Kristen yang bergerak di bidang pelayanan dan pendidikan ini dilakukan setiap hari minggu. Pada kesempatan itu, saya beserta teman kuliah dan satu staf dari yayasan mendapat tugas untuk mengajar anak-anak di sebuah desa yang letaknya cukup jauh dari kota Salatiga, tempat kami tinggal. Butuh waktu sekitar dua jam lebih untuk sampai ke sana. Selama perjalanan, medan yang dilalui cukup sulit karena kami harus melewati jalanan aspal yang telah rusak parah dan jalanan tanah yang cukup sempit. Kami juga harus bersahabat dengan hawa panas yang sangat menyengat akibat dari teriknya sinar matahari ditambah dengan banyaknya tanah tandus dan pohon kering di sepanjang perjalanan. Namun, hal tersebut tidak mengurangi semangat kami untuk bertemu dengan anak-anak yang akan kami ajar. Setelah melalui perjalanan yang cukup melelahkan, akhirnya kami tiba di salah satu rumah warga yang akan kami gunakan untuk kegiatan belajar mengajar. Beberapa anak telah berkumpul di dalam rumah itu dan ketika mereka melihat kedatangan kami, mereka langsung membentuk barisan memanjang dan satu per satu mulai memberikan salam kepada kami. Alangkah manisnya! Saya sangat kagum dengan sikap mereka yang sangat ramah yang dapat membuat siapa saja ingin tersenyum ketika melihat mereka. Saya mulai mengajak mereka bercerita tentang pelajaran mereka di sekolah. Ada sekitar dua puluh anak yang datang untuk belajar. Usia mereka bervariasi, dari usia TK hingga SMP. Melalui percakapan mereka, saya mengetahui bahwa sebagian besar dari mereka belum pernah diajarkan bahasa Inggris di sekolah. Anak-anak SMP pun belum mengetahui pelajaran bahasa Inggris tingkat dasar seperti berhitung dari satu hingga sepuluh, atau menulis kosakata sederhana lainnya. Mereka juga bercerita tentang harapan mereka ke depan untuk memiliki fasilitas belajar yang memadai dan memperoleh lebih banyak kesempatan lagi untuk belajar bahasa Inggris. Hal itulah yang membuat kami sadar betapa mereka sangat ingin belajar hal-hal baru, tetapi fasilitas yang ada masih jauh dari kata memadai. Saya pun bersyukur karena dari kegiatan ini, mereka mendapat kesempatan untuk mempelajari hal-hal baru tersebut. Waktu belajar dimulai. Kami mengawalinya dengan berdoa, dan sebagian besar dari mereka, yang berbeda keyakinan, ikut melipat tangan dan menutup mata mereka. Selesai berdoa, kami membagi mereka dalam kelompok kelas kecil dan kelas besar. Kelas kecil terdiri dari anak usia TK hingga kelas tiga SD, sedangkan kelas besar terdiri dari anak-anak kelas empat SD ke atas. Saya mendapat kesempatan untuk mengajar anak-anak kelas besar. Banyak hal yang saya coba ajarkan kepada mereka, mulai dari kosakata sederhana tentang binatang, mengerjakan soal, hingga bermain gim sederhana untuk mengasah kemampuan bahasa Inggris mereka. Rasa lelah dan capai tentu kami rasakan karena mengajar anak-anak seusia mereka bukanlah perkara yang mudah. Namun, pada saat seperti itulah, kami menyadari bahwa kegiatan tersebut kami lakukan untuk memuliakan nama Tuhan. Kami yakin dan percaya bahwa Tuhanlah yang akan memberi kekuatan yang membuat kami mampu untuk melakukannya dengan baik. Kegiatan hari itupun selesai. Kami bersyukur bahwa kegiatan mengajar itu dapat kami lakukan dengan cukup baik terlepas dari kekurangan dan kendala yang kami rasakan sewaktu mengajar. Semangat belajar dari anak-anak juga membuat kami terdorong untuk memberikan pengajaran yang lebih baik lagi pada masa yang akan datang. Kami sangat bersyukur karena Tuhan memberikan perlindungan dan kasih-Nya kepada anak-anak yang kami ajar sehingga mereka masih dapat bertumbuh dengan baik dan memperoleh kesempatan-kesempatan untuk mengembangkan pengetahuan mereka. K

title: Tuhan Menuntunku Mengenal Pribadi-Nya
title_zh: 神引导我认识祂自己
content: Karena dilahirkan dan dibesarkan dalam keluarga Katolik Roma, saya dididik dengan segala tata cara mereka semenjak kecil. Sejak usia yang sangat muda, saya terbiasa mengakui dosa-dosa saya, dengan teguh percaya bahwa dosa-dosa saya diampuni pada waktu pengakuan dosa. Sering kali, beban dosa saya menjadi begitu besar sehingga setelah pengakuan dosa dan merasa bahwa dosa-dosa saya hilang, saya kemudian berharap untuk segera mati sebelum saya berbuat dosa lagi. Namun, pemikiran ini hanya sebentar karena hal itu hanya berlangsung beberapa menit sebelum saya kemudian berbuat dosa lagi, baik dalam pemikiran maupun tindakan. Pada waktu Paskah, selama pembacaan kisah penderitaan Kristus, semua penderitaan-Nya, dan akhirnya kematian-Nya, terkadang saya berpikir, "Mengapa Dia membiarkan mereka membunuh-Nya? Mengapa Dia tidak menghindar dari situasi itu?" Karena Dia adalah Allah, Dia dapat melakukannya. Namun, saya tidak mendapat jawaban. Sering kali, saya akan berpikir, "Apa yang akan saya katakan kepada Allah ketika saya bertemu Dia dengan semua dosa saya?" Sebagai seorang remaja, beban dosa saya sangat besar dan sangat berat bagi saya. Saya tidak tahu di mana saya akan berada dalam keabadian, dan orang-orang yang saya tanyakan memiliki kebingungan yang sama dengan saya. "Di mana jawabannya? Siapa yang memiliki jawabannya? Agama apa yang benar?" Saya bertanya. Namun, saya tidak pernah meragukan bahwa Gereja Katolik Roma adalah jalan yang benar. Hanya, saya tidak dapat menemukan kedamaian. Setelah saya menikah, keadaannya sama. Kemudian, saya memikirkan Alkitab. Meskipun saya belum pernah melihat ke dalamnya, saya tahu isinya akan benar. Firman Allah akan memiliki jawaban untuk saya, jawaban atas pertanyaan saya. Ke mana saya pergi: ke surga? Ke neraka? Bagaimana saya dapat mengetahuinya? Jika saya menuju surga, baiklah. Akan tetapi, jika saya menuju neraka, apakah ada yang bisa saya lakukan? Dan, selama masa-masa ini, saya menjadi semakin religius. Akhirnya, pada November 1975, saya menyuarakan keinginan saya untuk memiliki Alkitab, untuk membaca sendiri firman Tuhan. Suami saya berjanji untuk membelikan saya Alkitab sebagai hadiah Natal. Pada 8 Desember, dua pria yang dikenal oleh suami saya datang ke rumah kami, berbicara kepada kami tentang Tuhan Yesus Kristus, dan mengatakan bahwa mereka mengetahui dengan pasti bahwa mereka akan pergi ke surga, dan itu adalah menurut Alkitab. Mereka meninggalkan kami dengan sebuah buku Injil Yohanes, menunjukkan kepada kami satu atau dua ayat dari Alkitab, dan kemudian pergi. Salah satu dari ayat-ayat itu adalah "Sesungguhnya Aku mengatakan kepadamu, orang yang mendengar perkataan-Ku dan percaya kepada Dia yang mengutus Aku memiliki hidup kekal, dan tidak masuk ke dalam penghakiman karena ia sudah pindah dari kematian ke kehidupan" (Yohanes 5:24, AYT). Saya memikirkan betapa bahagianya orang-orang itu, yang secara pasti mengetahui tempat mereka akan menghabiskan kekekalan. Tepat seminggu kemudian, pada 15 Desember, pada larut malam, saya duduk dan membaca buku kecil lain yang saya dapatkan, God's Way of Salvation (Jalan Keselamatan Allah - Red.). Saya memahami dari buku tersebut bahwa meskipun keselamatan itu gratis bagi saya dan tidak dapat diperoleh dengan cara apa pun, itu tentu membuat Allah membayar dengan mahal. Dia telah memberikan Anak-Nya yang terkasih untuk mati bagi dosa di salib Kalvari. Namun, saya masih bingung bagaimana cara mendapatkan keselamatan ini. Kemudian, saya memikirkan hal-hal yang saya percayai untuk membawa saya ke surga: Agama saya, saya dorong keluar. Agama tidak dapat membantu saya. Baptisan saya, saya membuangnya. Baptisan tidak dapat memberi kedamaian kepada saya. Hidup saya yang baik, melakukan yang terbaik yang saya bisa, saya buang. Bahkan, kebaikan saya tidak dapat mengambil beban dosa saya. Doa saya, saya menyingkirkannya. Doa adalah perbuatan "saya" juga, dan itu bukanlah jawaban. Gereja saya. Bahkan, gereja saya yang sangat saya andalkan tidak dapat membuat sa

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

title: Kembali Kepada Jalan Tuhan
title_zh: 回归主的道路
content: Nama saya Yoel, saya adalah seorang mahasiswa semester terakhir dari salah satu universitas swasta di Jawa Tengah. Saya dilahirkan dalam keluarga Kristen. Ibu dan Bapak saya cukup baik dalam membimbing saya untuk tetap dalam jalan Tuhan. Penyertaan Tuhan itu baik dalam kehidupan saya. Baiklah, saya akan ceritakan apa dosa yang sudah pernah saya lakukan. Rokok, pornografi, dan buang-buang waktu adalah keseharian saya pada waktu saya duduk di bangku SMU. Pada waktu itu, saya merasa ada yang kosong dalam hidup saya, tepatnya tidak ada gairah untuk mencapai suatu tujuan. Saya tidak merencanakan masa depan, pokoknya hidup terus mengalir. Sebenarnya, saya tertarik dengan dunia perfilman, saya ingin menjadi sutradara, tetapi ayah saya tidak mengizinkannya karena dia tidak melihat ada bakat seni dalam diri saya. Menurutnya, orang seni hanya akan mendapat uang atau pengakuan jika karyanya diterima. Kalau tidak mendapat pengakuan, ya "habis". Itulah perkataan ayah saya, saya masih ingat jelas. Menurut saya, dosa itu nikmat. Namun, saya juga sadar bahwa itu hanya kenikmatan sesaat. Saat saya masih SMU kelas satu, selama setahun saya merokok, tetapi saya benar-benar tidak dapat merasakan kenikmatannya. Mungkin itu hanya alat bagi saya supaya diterima oleh teman-teman saya. Saya suka mencoba hal baru, mungkin itu juga motivasi saya saat itu. Namun, jangan salah paham, teman-teman saya tidak pernah memaksa saya ikut merokok. Akhirnya, saya berhenti merokok saat kelas dua. Sebelumnya, sejak SMP kelas tiga, saya sudah kecanduan pornografi. Video porno begitu menarik bagi saya. Keinginan untuk melihat adegan dewasa itu sangat kuat. Ketika kuliah, pada tahun kedua, saya mulai berusaha serius untuk menghentikan kebiasaan tersebut. Saya mulai berpikir tentang dampak buruk pornografi secara serius. Menurut saya, sepertinya hanya saya yang ingin benar-benar lepas dari pornografi dalam lingkup pertemanan saya. Teman-teman saya sepertinya menerima hal itu sebagai sesuatu yang normal. Saya pun juga berusaha menerimanya sebagai sesuatu yang normal, tetapi saya tidak bisa berpikir seperti itu. Pasti ada dampak buruknya, saya yakin itu. Salah satu dampak buruk yang sudah saya rasakan adalah rendah diri. Saya selalu merasa diri saya itu "sampah". Dampak lainya adalah ketika saya melihat lawan jenis, saya akan cenderung menjadikannya objek seks. Itu sungguh menghancurkan martabat manusia sebagai makhluk yang berakal budi. Saya merasa kalau saya menonton video porno dan onani (ini sangat umum dalam dunia remaja), Tuhan akan membenci saya dan tidak menganggap saya lagi. Saya pernah berpikir untuk meninggalkan Tuhan dan hidup sesuka hati saya. Suatu saat, pernah saya berpikir bahwa saya sudah terlalu berdosa sehingga tidak bisa diperbaiki. Namun, Yesaya 1:18 menyadarkan saya bahwa Tuhan selalu menerima pertobatan manusia, tidak peduli seberapa buruk dosa yang sudah dilakukannya. Dalam kelemahan saya, Tuhan seolah-olah berkata, "Tidak apa-apa, Nak, bangun dan jangan berhenti." Pada tahun ketiga kuliah saya, sebenarnya saya sudah bisa lepas dari pornografi, dalam arti tidak kecanduan, tetapi tetap ada satu atau dua kali saya tergoda. Saya juga mengisi beberapa tahun dalam hidup saya kecanduan gim (game). Saat SMP, gim PS2 membuat saya menghabiskan uang jajan saya. Saat SMU dan kuliah, gim komputer membuat saya lupa waktu. Memang gim ini menjadi suatu pelampiasan akan rasa rendah diri saya. Selain bermain gim, aktivitas lain yang saya kerjakan adalah makan dan mandi. Saya tidak peduli akan hal lain. Tentu saja, sekarang saya menyesal, berapa banyak waktu yang saya buang. Alangkah baiknya jika dahulu saya melakukan sesuatu yang produktif, seperti mengasah kemampuan dalam bidang tertentu. Menyia-nyiakan waktu yang diberikan Tuhan adalah dosa, karena hidup kita menjadi tidak berguna. Saya juga pernah berjudi daring. title: Pertolongan yang Tidak Pernah Terlambat
title_zh: 永远不会迟到的帮助
content: Oleh: Odysius B. Temara Bersyukur untuk kasih karunia Tuhan yang selama ini tidak henti-hentinya saya rasakan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada kesempatan kali ini, saya ingin berbagi tentang kisah pengalaman hidup saya. Semasa kuliah, saya merasa bahwa saya adalah salah satu orang yang paling beruntung karena hampir selalu mendapatkan kemudahan dalam studi saya. Saya mendapatkan dosen-dosen yang ramah, teman-teman yang selalu mendukung saya, bahkan para staf akademik yang sangat bisa diajak bekerja sama. Semuanya berjalan sesuai dengan apa yang saya rancangkan sampai tiba-tiba segalanya berubah ketika saya menginjak semester akhir. Saya sangat terkejut ketika mengetahui bahwa saya diberi dosen pembimbing yang terkenal sangat sulit untuk penulisan skripsi saya. Beliau adalah salah satu dosen yang paling sibuk dan paling susah untuk dihubungi, terlebih untuk konsultasi. Pernah sampai tiga minggu beliau keluar kota, sakit, dan terlalu sibuk dengan tugas-tugas mengajar sehingga skripsi saya menjadi terbengkalai karena saya tidak bisa berkonsultasi dengan beliau. Ketika saya sedang berkonsultasi dengan beliau, sering kali beliau juga menyelipkan kalimat-kalimat sarkastik yang terkadang membuat saya lebih tertekan lagi. Seiring berjalannya waktu, teman-teman saya mulai lulus satu per satu, dan saya masih terjebak. Pada saat itu, saya merasa sangat kesal karena skripsi saya tidak kunjung selesai. Bukan karena saya yang malas-malasan, tetapi karena sulitnya menemui dosen pembimbing saya. Saya sempat mempertimbangkan untuk pindah pembimbing, tetapi rasanya sangat sayang kalau harus mulai dari awal lagi. Saya menceritakan keluh kesah saya kepada orang tua saya. Ayah saya menyarankan saya untuk lebih giat lagi berdoa, serahkan semuanya kepada Tuhan. Saya berdoa kepada Tuhan supaya Dia melembutkan hati dosen pembimbing saya dan juga memberi kekuatan dan kesabaran untuk saya dalam menghadapi beliau. Hari demi hari, saya berdoa dan sedikit demi sedikit tampak mulai terjadi perubahan pada sikap dosen pembimbing saya. Perubahan sikap itu tidak hanya terjadi kepada saya, tetapi juga kepada anak bimbingannya yang lain. Akhirnya, dengan proses yang cukup panjang, saya berhasil menyelesaikan skripsi saya dan lulus pada 12 Agustus 2014. Meskipun rancangan saya gagal untuk bisa lulus dalam 3,5 tahun, saya merasa bersyukur karena pertolongan Tuhan tidak pernah terlambat bagi saya sehingga saya masih bisa lulus tepat waktu. Sampai sekarang, saya senantiasa mengucap syukur kepada Tuhan atas segala yang Tuhan izinkan terjadi dalam kehidupan saya. Saya menyadari bahwa seberat apa pun permasalahan hidup yang saya hadapi, tangan kuat Tuhan akan selalu ada untuk menuntun saya melewatinya.

title: Merasakan Kasih Natal
title_zh: 感受圣诞节的爱
content: Natal merupakan liburan yang paling istimewa bagi ayah saya. Persiapan menjelang Natal, berbelanja hadiah, dan menghias rumah tidak membuatnya lelah - bahkan ia sangat menikmatinya. Ibu bercerita, ayah memperkenalkan saya dengan pohon Natal saya yang pertama waktu saya masih berusia sembilan hari. Pohon Natal itu kecil, tetapi setiap hiasan, lilin, dan untaian perada perak digantungnya dengan sangat teliti pada tempatnya, seolah-olah hanya ia yang dapat melakukannya. Setelah selesai, ayah mengangkat saya dari keranjang buaian dan menggendong saya supaya melihat hasil pekerjaan tangannya. Ayah masih menghias empat pohon Natal sesudah itu dan setiap kali pohonnya lebih besar dari tahun sebelumnya. Pada hari ia meninggal -- tak lama setelah menderita radang paru-paru -- ibu duduk dengan saya membicarakan Natal. "Madeline," katanya lembut, "Sinterklas akan memberikan hadiah untukmu, tetapi kita tidak mempunyai pohon dan hiasannya. Tahun ini pengeluaran kita sudah terlalu banyak." Besok hari Natal, tetapi sampai pagi ini tidak ada persiapan khusus untuk keesokah harinya, selain kebaktian pagi dan makan malam di rumah salah seorang anggota keluarga. Menjelang sore, telepon berbunyi dan ibu mengangkatnya. Tidak lama kemudian saya mendengar ibu berkata, "Anda baik sekali, tetapi rasanya kami akan melewatkan malam Natal di rumah. Natal ini pertama kali sejak ..." Lalu ibu dapat melanjutkan lagi, berterima kasih kepada penelepon itu sekali lagi dan menutup pembicaraan. "Siapa Bu?" tanya saya. "Salah seorang tetangga kita," kata ibu. "Ia mengundang kita malam ini. Ibu ... Ibu tidak bisa." Ibu diam saja hampir sepanjang hari. Sorenya, ibu berubah pendapat. Ia menelepon tetangga kami, mengatakan kami akan mampir sebentar. "Dia baik sekali," kata ibu kepada saya, "dan kita tidak mau dianggap tidak menghargainya." Setelah kami membunyikan bel pintu rumah tetangga kami, nyonya rumah menyambut dan mencium kami, lalu mengantar kami melewati serambi. Ruang tamu kelihatannya gelap, tetapi anehnya ada cahaya yang berwarna-warni. Ia mengajak kami masuk, dan saya melangkah ke dalam ruangan dan terperangah. Di sana, di tengah taburan lampu yang berwarna-warni dan bermacam-macam hiasan, lengkap dengan hadiah-hadiah yang dibungkus dengan kertas wama-warni yang cerah, berdiri sebuah pohon Natal yang indah sekali. Di sekeliling pohon itu duduk Ny. Abrams, Ny. Cohen, Ny. Blount, Ny. Dreyfus, sambil tersenyum lebar. "Selamat datang!" sapa mereka serempak. Sampai sekarang saya dapat memejamkan mata dan mengingat kisah tersebut dengan jelas. Sering ingatan itu menguatkan saya apabila keadaan memburuk, waktu saya meragukan hati manusia. Saya masih dapat merasakan kasih tetangga kami -- kaum ibu Yahudi yang mengambil risiko untuk melaksanakan tradisi yang tidak mereka kenal supaya seorang anak Kristen yang sudah tidak mempunyai ayah tetap dapat bergembira merayakan Natal. - Madeline Weatherford | Dipublikasikan | : | http://natal.sabda.org |

content:
2026년 다니엘기도회 19일차 강사: 정주호 스타트레인 대표(한동대 겸임교수) 내 안에 잠든 영적 근육을 깨워라 본문: 고린도전서 10장 31절

1. 하나님을 원망하던 청년

저는 평생 사람들의 근육을 단련하는 일을 해 왔습니다. 그러나 하나님을 만나고 깨달았습니다. 사람에게는 몸을 지탱하는 근육만큼이나 삶을 지탱하는 믿음의 근육이 필요하다는 사실입니다.

어린 시절 저는 하나님을 향한 분노가 많았습니다. 가난했고, 가진 것도 배운 것도 없었습니다. 특히 아버지로부터 받은 상처가 깊었습니다. 교회에서는 하나님이 사랑이시며 우리의 아버지라고 가르쳤지만, 그 말은 제게 위로가 아니라 고통이었습니다.

아버지에게 상처받은 사람에게 ‘하나님 아버지’라는 표현은 또 다른 상처가 될 수 있습니다. 저 역시 하나님이 아버지라면 내가 경험한 아버지와 무엇이 다른지 이해할 수 없었습니다.

그래서 월요일마다 아무도 없는 교회를 찾아갔습니다. 돌멩이를 주워 교회 십자가를 향해 던졌습니다. 하나님이 정말 계신다면 나타나 보시라는 마음이었습니다. 그러면서도 혹시 벌을 받을까 두려웠습니다.

어릴 때부터 교회에 다니기는 했습니다. 부활절이면 달걀을 주고, 친구를 데려가면 연필과 필통을 받을 수 있었기 때문입니다. 그러나 제 안에는 진정한 믿음이 없었습니다. 가장 힘들었던 순간 하나님께 도와 달라고 울부짖었지만 아무런 응답도 느끼지 못했습니다.

어려운 현실을 벗어나고 싶어 캐나다로 떠났습니다. 친척이 운영하는 세탁소에서 일하고, 잔디를 깎고, 대리운전과 공장 일도 했습니다. 그러나 해외 생활 역시 쉽지 않았습니다. 경제적으로 어려웠고, 신분도 불안정했습니다. 여러 교회를 옮겨 다녔지만, 어느 곳에도 정착하지 못했습니다.

그때 제가 붙잡은 것은 운동이었습니다. 화가 날 때마다 아령을 들었습니다. 운동을 하면 분노가 어느 정도 가라앉았습니다. 몸은 점점 단단해졌지만, 마음은 오히려 메말라 갔습니다.

저는 세례를 네 번이나 받았습니다. 믿음이 확고해서가 아니었습니다. 믿음이 부족하니 세례라도 여러 번 받아 두면 안전하지 않을까 하는 어리석은 생각 때문이었습니다.

대학 진학도 순탄하지 않았습니다. 여러 차례 입시에 실패했고, 어렵게 지방 전문대학에 들어갔습니다. 수능시험 도중 공부하기 싫어 시험장을 나와 당구장으로 향했던 적도 있습니다.

그런 제가 훗날 대학에서 학생들을 가르치는 교수가 되었습니다. 그래서 청년들에게 말하고 싶습니다. 지금의 성적이 여러분 인생의 전부는 아닙니다. 하나님은 부족하고 연약한 사람도 사용하실 수 있습니다.

한때는 믿음도 없이 성지순례를 떠났습니다. 예루살렘과 갈릴리를 방문했지만, 영적인 깨달음보다는 여행 자체가 즐거웠습니다. 갈릴리에서 이른바 베드로 물고기를 네 마리나 먹었던 기억이 더 선명했습니다. 그러나 방황하는 동안에도 하나님이 정말 계신다면 한번 제대로 만나 보고 싶다는 생각은 사라지지 않았습니다.

2. 하나님께 따지러 갔다가 예수님을 만나다

한국으로 돌아온 뒤에도 아버지의 빚은 남아 있었고, 저는 운동을 가르치며 돈을 벌어야 했습니다. 그러던 어느 날 하나님이 계신지 직접 확인하고 싶었습니다. 주변에서 가장 뜨겁게 기도한다는 교회를 찾아갔습니다. 약 300명의 청년들이 모여 통성기도를 하고 있었습니다.

저는 기도하러 간 것이 아니었습니다. 하나님께 따지러 갔습니다.

왜 나를 이렇게 힘들게 하셨느냐고, 왜 우리 가정은 고통받아야 했느냐고 원망하고 싶었습니다. 사람들이 큰 소리로 기도하는 틈을 타 저도 하나님을 향해 온갖 불평과 욕설을 쏟아냈습니다. 그런데 그 순간 제 마음 깊은 곳에 뜻밖의 감동이 밀려왔습니다.

“너는 죄인이다.”

처음에는 죄책감이라고 생각했습니다. 내가 교회에 와서 하나님을 욕했으니 양심이 찔리는 것이라고 여겼습니다. 그러나 또 다른 감동이 찾아왔습니다.

“너는 나의 아들 예수를 모른다.”

그 순간 제 안에서 무언가 무너져 내렸습니다. 평생 하나님을 원망하고 불신했던 제가 사실은 예수님을 제대로 알지 못했다는 사실을 깨달았습니다.

눈물이 쏟아졌습니다. 얼굴이 뜨겁게 느껴질 만큼 울었습니다. 다른 사람들이 기도를 마치고 돌아간 뒤에도 저는 자리에서 일어나지 못했습니다. 그날 저는 처음으로 하나님을 인격적으로 만났다고 고백할 수 있게 되었습니다.

다음 날 아침 출근하면서도 전날의 경험이 진짜였는지 의심스러웠습니다. 그런데 길을 걷다가 나무에서 떨어지는 낙엽을 보며 갑자기 눈물이 났습니다. 길가의 작은 풀을 보아도, 지나가는 고양이를 보아도 마음이 움직였습니다.

그때 제 마음에 이런 감동이 찾아왔습니다. ‘이 모든 것을 내가 너를 위해 준비했다. 내가 너를 사랑한다.’

이전에는 세상을 보면서 분노했지만, 이제는 작은 생명에서도 하나님의 사랑을 느끼기 시작했습니다. 구급차가 지나가면 그 안에 있는 환자를 위해 기도했습니다. 전혀 모르는 사람의 아픔이 제 마음에 들어오기 시작했습니다.

하나님을 만난 뒤 가장 크게 달라진 것은, 환경이 아니라 사람을 바라보는 제 마음이었습니다.

3. 비우고, 채우고, 부르시다

하나님을 믿게 되었지만 새로운 고민이 생겼습니다. 이제 어떻게 살아야 하는지 알 수 없었습니다. 믿음을 갖는 것과 자신의 사명을 발견하는 것은 다른 문제였습니다.

성경을 읽기 시작했지만, 창세기부터 이해하기 어려웠습니다. 그래서 예수님의 삶을 먼저 알아야겠다는 생각으로 마태복음, 마가복음, 누가복음, 요한복음을 반복해서 읽었습니다.

그러던 중 3일 동안 기도하는 수련회에 참석했습니다.

첫날 저는 하나님께 물질적 축복을 구했습니다. 가진 것도 없고 배운 것도 부족하니 이제는 제 삶을 채워 달라고 기도했습니다. 그런데 마음에 찾아온 말씀은 예상과 달랐습니다.

“비워라.”

이미 가진 것이 없는데 무엇을 더 비우라는 것인지 답답했습니다. 그러나 기도하면서 깨달았습니다. 비워야 할 것은 통장에 있는 돈이 아니라 마음속에 가득한 욕심이었습니다. 세상을 향한 집착, 성공에 대한 갈망, 인정받고 싶은 마음이었습니다.

둘째 날에는 또 다른 감동이 찾아왔습니다.

“채워라.”

이번에는 하나님께서 물질을 채워 주시려는 줄 알았습니다. 그러나 제가 깨달은 것은 하나님의 마음으로 자신을 채우라는 뜻이었습니다.

셋째 날에는 이런 감동을 받았습니다.

“부르겠다.”

저는 어느 기업의 회장이나 성공한 사업가가 저를 부르려는 것인지 기대했습니다. 그러나 시간이 지나면서 그것이 세상의 성공을 향한 부름이 아니라 하나님께서 맡기실 사명을 향한 부르심임을 알게 되었습니다.

비움, 채움, 부르심. 이 세 가지는 이후 제 인생을 바꾸는 중요한 과정이 되었습니다.

4. 174kg의 한 영혼을 향한 부르심

수련회에서 돌아온 뒤 텔레비전을 보다가, 몸무게가 174kg에 이르는 한 여성을 보았습니다.

그 순간 설명하기 어려운 감동이 밀려왔습니다. 저분을 찾아가 도와야겠다는 생각이 마음을 떠나지 않았습니다.

저는 운동을 가르치는 트레이너였습니다. 그러나 그 여성을 돕기 위해, 안정적인 직장을 포기해야 했습니다. 결국 사표를 냈습니다. 그 여성이 살고 있는 곳은 경기도 연천이었습니다. 당시 교통편이 불편해 왕복하는 데 약 다섯 시간이 걸렸습니다.

처음 찾아갔을 때 문을 열어주지 않았습니다. 낯선 청년이 찾아와 운동을 가르쳐 주겠다고 하니, 당연히 경계했을 것입니다. 하지만 포기하지 않았습니다. 찾아가고 또 찾아갔습니다. 그렇게 7개월이 흘렀습니다. 저는 문 앞에서 그분을 위해 기도했습니다.

마침내 문이 열렸습니다.

“청년, 나 좀 도와줘요.”

그런데 막상 들어가 보니, 제가 감당할 수 있는 상황이 아니었습니다. 지금까지 운동을 가르치며 체중을 10kg 정도 감량하도록 도운 경험은 있었지만, 이분은 훨씬 큰 도움이 필요했습니다.

저는 그분의 손을 잡고 울면서 기도했습니다. 제 능력으로는 어렵다는 사실을 깨달았기 때문입니다. 운동기구를 살 돈도 없었습니다. 그래서 주변에서 구할 수 있는 물통과 배추 등을 활용해 운동했습니다. 손뼉을 치고, 팔을 들어 올리고, 몸을 조금씩 움직이는 것부터 시작했습니다.

무엇보다 우리는 운동만 하지 않았습니다. 먼저 서로의 삶을 이야기했습니다. 지난 한

title: “주여, 저희들을 긍휼히 여겨 주옵소서”… 기독문화선교회 신바람힐링성회
summary: 사단법인 기독문화선교회(고문 조병창 목사, 대표회장 강형규 목사, 상임대표 서정형)가 오는 12월 7일부터 12일까지 오산리최자실기념금식기도원 대성전에서 ‘신바람힐링성회’를 개최한다. ‘주여! 저희들을 긍휼히 여겨 주옵소서!’를 주제로 열리는 이번 성회는 시편 103편 13~19절 말씀을 중심으로 진행된다. 말씀 선포를 비롯해 찬양과 간증, 건강 강의 등을 함께 구성해 신앙과 삶에 지친 성도들이 영적 회복과 새로운 힘을 얻도록 마련했다. 특히 한국교회 금식기도 운동의 상징적인 공간인 오산리최자실기념금식기도원에서 6일간 성회를 이어간다는 점에서 의미를 더한다. 선교회는 이번 집회를 일회성 행사가 아닌 교회와 성도들의 영적 회복을 위한 집중 사역으로 준비하고 있다.
summary_zh: 社团法人基督教文化宣教团（顾问赵炳昌牧师、代表会长姜亨圭牧师、常任代表徐正亨）将于12月7日至12日在梧山里崔慈实纪念禁食祷告院的大圣殿举办“神风治愈大会”。“主啊！求您怜悯我们！”本次圣会以这一主题举行，将围绕诗篇103篇13-19节的经文展开。大会将包括宣讲神的话语、赞美、见证分享以及健康讲座等内容，旨在帮助在信仰和生活中感到疲惫的信徒获得属灵的恢复和新的力量。特别值得一提的是，本次大会将在韩国教会禁食祷告运动的标志性场所——梧山里崔慈实纪念禁食祷告院连续举行6天。宣道会正在筹备本次聚会，将其定位为一项旨在促进教会和信徒灵性复兴的集中性事工，而非一次性的活动。
title_zh: “主啊，求您怜悯我们”……基督教文化宣教会的喜乐医治布道会
content:
사단법인 기독문화선교회(고문 조병창 목사, 대표회장 강형규 목사, 상임대표 서정형)가 오는 12월 7일부터 12일까지 오산리최자실기념금식기도원 대성전에서 ‘신바람힐링성회’를 개최한다.

‘주여! 저희들을 긍휼히 여겨 주옵소서!’를 주제로 열리는 이번 성회는 시편 103편 13~19절 말씀을 중심으로 진행된다. 말씀 선포를 비롯해 찬양과 간증, 건강 강의 등을 함께 구성해 신앙과 삶에 지친 성도들이 영적 회복과 새로운 힘을 얻도록 마련했다.

특히 한국교회 금식기도 운동의 상징적인 공간인 오산리최자실기념금식기도원에서 6일간 성회를 이어간다는 점에서 의미를 더한다. 선교회는 이번 집회를 일회성 행사가 아닌 교회와 성도들의 영적 회복을 위한 집중 사역으로 준비하고 있다.

title: 세계 교회 붉은빛으로 물들다… 박해받는 기독교인 위한 ‘붉은 주간’

summary_zh: 世界各地的教堂、大教堂和公共建筑被染成了红色。11月，世界各国正在开展“红色周”（Red Week）活动，以纪念因捍卫信仰而遭受迫害和暴力的基督徒，并呼吁国际社会声援他们。此次活动由国际天主教慈善组织“援助受难教会”（Aid to the Church in Need，以下简称ACN）主办，将从11月15日（以下均为当地时间）持续至22日，世界各地在18日左右举办了各种纪念活动。“红色周”活动始于2015年，是一项国际性的宗教自由运动，旨在通过象征殉道者鲜血的红色灯光，让人们了解受迫害基督徒的真实处境。据ACN称，今年的活动将有来自世界各地的12.5万多人参与，130座大教堂以及约1000座教堂和建筑将亮起红色灯光。
title_zh: 世界各地的教堂被染成红色……为受迫害的基督徒举办“红色周”活动
content:
세계 곳곳의 교회와 대성당, 공공건물이 붉은빛으로 물들었다. 신앙을 지키다 박해와 폭력에 노출된 기독교인들을 기억하고, 이들을 위한 국제사회의 연대를 촉구하는 ‘레드 위크’(Red Week) 캠페인이 11월 세계 각국에서 진행되고 있다.

국제 가톨릭 구호단체 ‘에이드 투 더 처치 인 니드’(Aid to the Church in Need, 이하 ACN)이 주관하는 이번 캠페인은 11월 15일(이하 현지시각)부터 22일까지 이어지며, 18일을 중심으로 세계 각국에서 다양한 기념행사가 열렸다. 2015년 시작된 레드 위크는 순교자들의 피를 상징하는 붉은색 조명을 통해 박해받는 기독교인들의 현실을 알리는 국제적인 종교자유 캠페인이다.

ACN에 따르면 올해 행사에는 전 세계 12만5,000명 이상이 참여하며, 130개 대성당과 약 1,000개의 교회 및 건축물이 붉은빛으로 밝혀질 예정이다. 교회 조명 행사뿐 아니라 기도회와 박해 생존자 증언, 공개 행사, 학교 프로그램 등도 마련돼 신앙 때문에 고통받는 기독교인들과 연대하는 시간을 갖는다.

프랑스에서는 파리 노트르담 대성당과 사크레쾨르 대성당, 샤르트르 대성당 등 주요 종교·역사 건축물이 붉은빛으로 밝혀졌다. 프랑스 전역에서는 약 80개 교회와 장소가 참여하고 4,000여 명의 자원봉사자가 농촌 지역까지 캠페인을 알리고 있다. 스페인에서도 250개가 넘는 교회와 대성당, 기념물 및 공공건물이 참여했으며, 영국에서는 런던 사우스워크의 성 조지 대성당에서 특별 미사가 열렸다. 아일랜드의 녹 대성당과 오스트리아 대통령궁 등도 캠페인에 동참했다.

이번 행사는 세계 기독교 박해 상황이 악화하고 있다는 우려 속에서 진행됐다. ACN의 최근 종교자유 보고서에 따르면 전 세계 약 4억1,300만 명의 기독교인이 종교자유에 대한 심각한 침해가 발생하는 국가에 살고 있으며, 약 2억2,000만 명은 직접적인 박해에 노출돼 있다. 특히 ACN이 집중적으로 관찰한 18개국에서는 지난 2년간 기독교인의 종교자유 상황이 개선되지 않았으며, 절반이 넘는 국가에서 상황이 악화한 것으로 나타났다.

보고서는 극단주의 폭력과 권위주의 정부, 종교적 민족주의가 기독교 공동체에 대한 압박을 가중하고 있다고 지적했다. 아프리카와 아시아 일부 지역에서는 무력 분쟁과 종교적 폭력으로 기독교인들이 거주지를 떠나는 상황도 이어지고 있다. 중동에서는 정치적 혼란과 전쟁이 지속되면서 기독교 신앙의 역사적 중심지에서 공동체의 존속 자체가 위협받고 있다는 우려도 제기됐다.

ACN 국제본부 레지나 린치 대표는 영상 메시지를 통해 “우리는 순교자들의 피를 상징하는 붉은색으로 교회와 건물들을 밝히고 있다”며 “그들은 종종 외로움과 고립감을 느끼며 희망이 필요하다. 우리가 드리는 기도를 통해 그들에게 희망을 전할 수 있다”고 말했다.

캠페인은 11월 23일 프랑스 스트라스부르 유럽의회 건물 점등 행사로도 이어질 예정이다. 필리핀에서는 주교회의가 11월 25일을 레드 웬즈데이로 지정했으며, 전국 87개 교구가 참여해 박해받는 기독교인을 위한 기도와 특별 헌금을 진행할 계획이다.
